# RASQ-Ai

> Trustworthy visual test automation: zero-DOM optical capture, requirements-to-test traceability, execution evidence, and evidence-based reporting. This file is for external AI agents that want to USE the running application. For agents editing the source code, see MASTER_PROMPT.md / CONTEXT_MEMORY.md instead.

## Authentication

All endpoints except `GET /api/health` and `GET /api/openapi.json` require either the single-operator browser session (same-origin UI) or, for external agents, a scoped API key:

```
Authorization: Bearer rasq_<random>
```

Keys are created by the operator via `POST /api/agent-keys` or `npm run agent:key`, stored as SHA-256 hashes, shown once, revocable, optionally expiring. Each key carries scopes; requests without a required scope get `403 insufficient_scope`. An invalid/revoked/expired key gets `401 invalid_api_key` and is never downgraded to operator access.

## Discovery

- OpenAPI 3.1: `GET /api/openapi.json` (public) — every operation lists its `x-rasq-scope`.
- Full guide with curl recipes, error codes and safety rules: `AGENT_GUIDE.md` at the repository root.
- Project partition: keys may be minted with `projectIds` (foreign-project artifacts answer 404; lists filter silently). Mint with `npm run agent:key -- --name x --preset --projects <id1>,<id2> [--daily-budget N]`.
- Audit: `GET /api/audit?format=csv` (operator only) exports the append-only trail; retention via `RASQ_AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS` (default 180d, irreversible).
- Webhooks: terminal events (`run.completed`, `desktop.run.completed`, `performance.run.completed`, `webhook.test`) can be pushed to a registered HTTPS receiver; operator-only setup via `POST /api/webhooks` (secret `whsec_…` shown once). Deliveries are signed `x-rasq-signature: v1=hex(HMAC_SHA256(secret, "<ts>.<rawBody>"))` — verify before trusting.
- MCP: a stdio MCP server (`npm run mcp`, env `RASQ_AI_URL` + `RASQ_API_KEY`) exposes the read + safe-generation subset as tools; it is a thin adapter over this same HTTP API, so scopes/audit/rate-limits apply unchanged.

## Capability map (scopes)

Read: projects:read, screens:read, requirements:read, tests:read, workflows:read, runs:read, reports:read, performance:read, settings:read, desktop:read.
Generate: projects:write, screens:write, requirements:write, tests:generate, workflows:write, reports:generate, settings:write, providers:write, ai:scan, capture:run, performance:plan.
Execution (grant deliberately): runs:start:dry-run, runs:start:playwright, performance:load, desktop:attend, desktop:confirm, desktop:revoke.
Deletion (grant deliberately): delete:artifacts.

Recommended starting set: projects:read, screens:read, requirements:read, tests:read, tests:generate, workflows:read, workflows:write, runs:read, runs:start:dry-run, reports:read.

## Canonical pipeline

1. `GET /api/projects` → pick a project id.
2. `POST /api/requirements` (upload/paste SRS) or `POST /api/capture` + screen analysis for visual anchors.
3. `POST /api/tests` → generate traceable cases. NOTE: SRS generation REPLACES the project's case set unless `replace:false`. Visual generation appends.
4. `POST /api/workflows` ({ projectId, mode:"generate" }) → runnable n8n-shaped workflow.
5. `POST /api/runs` { workflowId, mode:"dry-run" } → validates structure only, executes nothing. Poll `GET /api/runs/{id}` until `status` is terminal.
6. `POST /api/runs` { workflowId, mode:"playwright" } → real browser execution (needs `runs:start:playwright`).
7. `POST /api/reports` → Markdown report built only from recorded data.

## Rules agents must follow

- Dry-run first; real execution is an explicit operator decision.
- `manualReview` assertions yield `needs-review`, never a pass.
- Never invent requirement IDs, selectors, or outcomes; use only returned artifacts.
- Desktop (RobotJS) input is attended: preflight → `awaiting-operator-confirmation` → operator confirms. Never confirm on an operator's behalf unless granted the desktop:confirm scope, and only with explicit instruction.
- Load tests (`performance:load`) only against targets on `RASQ_JMETER_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`, and only when authorized.
- Send `Idempotency-Key` on POST /api/runs, /api/tests, /api/workflows; replays return the stored response with `idempotent-replay: true`.
- Rate limits are database-backed (default 120/min, `RASQ_AGENT_RATE_LIMIT`); per-key per-UTC-day mutation budgets may be set at mint time (`--daily-budget`); over-limit → 429 (`rate_limited` / `daily_budget_exceeded`); limiter failure → 503 (fail-closed).
- Prefer webhooks for completion signals when registered; otherwise poll `GET /api/runs/{id}` (no event stream exists).
- Errors are `{ "error": string, "code"?: string }`. Back off on `429 rate_limited`; do not retry `403 insufficient_scope` without an operator granting the scope.
- Generated artifacts are not execution evidence. Reports distinguish them; keep that distinction in your outputs.
